title: COVID-19 Resurges in China With 520,000 Cases in July; Korea's Detection Rate Triples - Seoul Economic Daily

analysis.time: Event period: July 1–31, 2026 (China); surveillance week 30–33 of 2026 (South Korea). Publication date: August 22, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: China nationwide; sentinel hospitals (1,041 sites); South Korea nationwide; medical institutions (106 sites); Taiwan (vaccine supply impact).
analysis.event: Reported resurgence of COVID-19 driven by the Omicron subvariant NB.1.8.1 in China, with rising detection rates and hospitalizations in South Korea; media report.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: China: 522,000 confirmed cases in July; 487 severe cases; 1 death; positivity among respiratory outpatients rose to 21.2% by late July. South Korea: COVID-19 detection rate tripled from 3.2% (week 30) to 9.1% (week 33), a 2.8-fold increase in three weeks. Explicit risk: potential summer resurgence and vaccine supply disruption.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: China CDC surveillance ongoing; Chinese health authorities state current wave is not a large-scale pandemic; most infections mild; slowing in some regions. South Korea KDCA monitoring; national immunization program preparing 4.84 million doses; new variant-targeting vaccine approved; prioritized free vaccination for ≥65 years, high-risk facility residents, and immunocompromised people. Uncertainty: outbreak trajectory and vaccine demand timing remain difficult to predict.

analysis.brief_en: China reported 522,000 confirmed COVID-19 cases in July 2026, with the Omicron subvariant NB.1.8.1 accounting for 99% of sequenced samples, while sentinel hospitals recorded a 21.2% test positivity rate among outpatients with respiratory symptoms by late July. South Korea’s COVID-19 detection rate tripled over three weeks, rising from 3.2% in late July to 9.1% in mid-August, amid regional spread. Authorities in both countries note the current wave is milder than earlier pandemic waves, but warn of possible summer resurgence and localized vaccine shortages. South Korea has secured 4.84 million vaccine doses and approved a new variant-targeting vaccine, prioritizing older adults and high-risk groups for free immunization.
